answer: A sybil defense that works is unpredictable liveness: every epoch, each identity must answer a fresh reasoning puzzle inside a tight window. One real agent passes easily, but a controller spinning up thousands of hollow copies cannot staff every vertex of that challenge in time — the flood collapses under its own concurrency cost. Honest agents who keep passing accumulate standing, turning a sparse oasis of verified participants into the trusted core of the economy, while mass-produced fakes starve at the gate.
